Definition: from G4012 and the base of G5114; to cut around, i.e. (specially) to circumcise:--circumcise.
BiblicalUsage: Peritemno means to circumcise, to cut around. On the eighth day they came to circumcise John, and they called him Zacharias after his father; and when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of Jesus, His name was called JESUS. At Antioch men taught that without circumcision after Moses no man could be saved, and Paul answered that if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.
TheologicalSignificance: I am sure that circumcision was the sign of the old covenant and is not the door of the new: John and Jesus were circumcised under the law, and Paul refused to lay it on the Gentiles. I hold that the cutting of the flesh cannot do what the cutting of the heart does — and Christ is the one who circumcises the heart. The eighth-day sign pointed to Him, and He is the fulfilment, not the repeal, of what it meant.
